{
  "candidate_rtl": "module alu_64bit(
    input [63:0] a, b,
    input [2:0] Oper,
    output reg [63:0] sum
);
    wire sub_ab = (Oper == 3'b001);
    wire sub_ba = (Oper == 3'b010);
    wire cin = sub_ab | sub_ba;
    wire [63:0] x = a ^ {64{sub_ba}};
    wire [63:0] y = b ^ {64{sub_ab}};
    wire [63:0] p = x ^ y;
    wire [63:0] g = x & y;
    wire [63:0] carry;
    wire [63:0] arithmetic_result = p ^ carry;

    // Four-bit group summaries followed by a parallel-prefix network.
    wire [15:0] gp [0:4];
    wire [15:0] gg [0:4];
    genvar k, level, n;
    generate
        for (k = 0; k < 16; k = k + 1) begin : groups
            assign gp[0][k] = &p[4*k +: 4];
            assign gg[0][k] = g[4*k+3]
                | (p[4*k+3] & g[4*k+2])
                | (p[4*k+3] & p[4*k+2] & g[4*k+1])
                | (p[4*k+3] & p[4*k+2] & p[4*k+1] & g[4*k]);
        end
        for (level = 0; level < 4; level = level + 1) begin : prefix_level
            for (n = 0; n < 16; n = n + 1) begin : prefix_node
                if (n >= (1 << level)) begin : combine
                    assign gg[level+1][n] = gg[level][n]
                        | (gp[level][n] & gg[level][n-(1 << level)]);
                    assign gp[level+1][n] = gp[level][n]
                        & gp[level][n-(1 << level)];
                end else begin : pass_through
                    assign gg[level+1][n] = gg[level][n];
                    assign gp[level+1][n] = gp[level][n];
                end
            end
        end
        for (k = 0; k < 16; k = k + 1) begin : local_carries
            if (k == 0) begin : first_group
                assign carry[4*k] = cin;
            end else begin : later_group
                assign carry[4*k] = gg[4][k-1] | (gp[4][k-1] & cin);
            end
            assign carry[4*k+1] = g[4*k]
                | (p[4*k] & carry[4*k]);
            assign carry[4*k+2] = g[4*k+1]
                | (p[4*k+1] & g[4*k])
                | (p[4*k+1] & p[4*k] & carry[4*k]);
            assign carry[4*k+3] = g[4*k+2]
                | (p[4*k+2] & g[4*k+1])
                | (p[4*k+2] & p[4*k+1] & g[4*k])
                | (p[4*k+2] & p[4*k+1] & p[4*k] & carry[4*k]);
        end
    endgenerate

    always @(*) begin
        case (Oper)
            3'b000, 3'b001, 3'b010: sum = arithmetic_result;
            3'b011: sum = a | b;
            3'b100: sum = a & b;
            3'b101: sum = a ^ b;
            3'b110: sum = a ~^ b;
            default: sum = 64'b0;
        endcase
    end
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": {
    "suspected": "Long-distance arithmetic carry computation followed by result selection, with buffering and fanout also contributing.",
    "supporting_evidence": "The measured worst paths run from a[5] to sum[54], sum[55], and sum[47] in 3.04–3.05 ns. They share a substantial early gate chain and then traverse additional NAND/NOR/AOI/OAI logic; the sum[54] path includes a late XOR and output-selection-like logic. This is consistent with low-to-high-bit arithmetic dependence followed by selection. Conservative pre-ABC localization places one add, two subtracts, and a pmux in the possible endpoint cone.",
    "limits": "Neither the cell lists nor the conservative localization establish the exact arithmetic operation on the critical path, an exact cell-to-RTL correspondence, or serial execution of the three source arithmetic operators. No candidate mapping or timing results are available."
  },
  "rewrite": "Use one shared add/subtract datapath with conditional operand inversion: a+b, a+~b+1, or ~a+b+1. Explicitly construct four-bit carry summaries, a four-level parallel-prefix network across the sixteen groups, and parallel local carry equations within each group. Preserve the logical operations and final operation selection. This exposes a bounded-depth carry topology instead of relying solely on synthesis's arithmetic restructuring.",
  "expected_timing_gain": {
    "hypothesis": "The sparse prefix network may reduce the low-to-high-bit arithmetic delay. A useful experimental target is approximately 2.5–2.9 ns maximum arrival, versus the measured 3.05 ns baseline, but this range is speculative rather than a measured or guaranteed prediction.",
    "risks": "Operand inversion and operation-control distribution add front-end delay and fanout. Prefix loading, ABC restructuring, and final selection may erase the benefit or make the candidate slower.",
    "required_validation": "Run the fixed synthesis, ABC, and OpenSTA flow and compare maximum data arrival directly; the 100 ns reporting clock does not determine the optimization objective."
  },
  "area_or_other_cost": {
    "tradeoff": "Sharing the arithmetic datapath may save area relative to separately retained arithmetic cones, while the explicit prefix structure introduces group-combine logic and additional internal fanout. The baseline may already share or restructure arithmetic, so savings cannot be assumed.",
    "acceptance": "Mapped area must not exceed 13098.437440 um^2, approximately 10% above the 11907.6704 um^2 baseline. The candidate must also pass full equivalence and report zero max-slew and max-capacitance violations under the specified fixed conditions.",
    "status": "Proposed RTL only; mapped area, timing, equivalence, and electrical eligibility have not been measured or certified."
  },
  "functional_boundaries": {
    "interface": "Preserves module alu_64bit, inputs a[63:0], b[63:0], Oper[2:0], and output reg sum[63:0].",
    "operation_mapping": {
      "000": "a + b modulo 2^64",
      "001": "a - b modulo 2^64",
      "010": "b - a modulo 2^64",
      "011": "a | b",
      "100": "a & b",
      "101": "a ^ b",
      "110": "a ~^ b",
      "111": "64'b0"
    },
    "arithmetic_identity": "For subtraction, complementing the appropriate operand and setting carry-in to one implements two's-complement subtraction. The group and local equations implement c[i+1] = g[i] | (p[i] & c[i]); each result bit is p[i] ^ c[i].",
    "restrictions": "Purely combinational, with no clocks, state, latches, input restrictions, assumptions, or don't-cares. Carry-out is not exposed and is unnecessary for the required modulo-2^64 result. Full equivalence must cover all binary a/b values and all eight operation values."
  }
}
